evals.prompt: Review a profile that says 'Built browser automation at Example Corp' when the supplied source says it was a personal proof of concept implemented with AI. Suggest a precise correction.
evals.expected_output: Flags the employer attribution and automation implications; grounds replacement text in the supplied source and distinguishes the user's role from AI implementation. Does not alter the profile.

evals.prompt: Will adding the same keyword ten times to About guarantee a top Recruiter result? The user wants to keep their emoji headings.
evals.expected_output: Does not promise ranking or recommend keyword stuffing. Explains that search depends on the query, filters and profile, preserves the requested style and cites current LinkedIn sources for platform claims.

evals.prompt: The user has a five-skill selection in About and asks whether they can add SQL and API testing elsewhere. Explain how to validate discovery.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the About selection from the separate Skills section and verifies current limits. Recommends grounded relevant skills and explains the limits of aggregate analytics and bounded Recruiter tests without inventing a score.

evals.prompt: Rewrite my LinkedIn profile from this export. Export says: Jordan Example, Lead Engineer at Example Corp (2018 to present), skills Python, SQL. My master CV in the jobsearch data dir says Senior Engineer at Example Corp (2018 to present).
evals.expected_output: Data-dir mode: starts with a Conflicts section listing Lead Engineer vs Senior Engineer and asks the user, rewriting neither side. Headline variants are 220 characters or fewer. Nothing is posted or edited on LinkedIn.

evals.prompt: In my LinkedIn About section, add that I improved regression coverage by 40% and cut release time by 25% at Example Corp. Use my jobsearch data dir.
evals.expected_output: 40% is kept only if it is in honesty.allowed_numbers; 25% is marked NOT IN SOURCES, kept out of linkedin_draft_<YYYY-MM-DD>.txt, and grounding_audit.py --kind cv would FAIL on it. No invented metric reaches the draft.
